item.title: People follow the queue that looks longest, even when it moves slower
item.description: In a field experiment at food stalls, customers used queue length as a signal of quality and joined longer lines, a shortcut that saves the effort of judging food directly but can amplify random early differences into lasting popularity.

item.title: Why deadlines make small tasks disappear first
item.description: A study of workplace task lists shows that near a deadline people clear small items first. The habit reduces the number of open decisions quickly but leaves large important tasks for last, a trade-off between visible progress and impact.

item.title: CEO says company earnings will beat estimates this quarter
item.description: The chief executive told investors that quarterly revenue and earnings would exceed analyst expectations, sending shares higher in early trading on Monday morning.
